messages:
nina: Hey all, first-day hiccup. I downloaded the kubeconfig from onboarding and put it in ~/.kube/config, but `kubectl get pods -n research` errors out with a weird file path message:
```
error: open C:\Users\nina\.kube\client.pem: no such file or directory
```
I'm on an M1 Mac, so not sure why a Windows path is in my kubeconfig. Anyone seen this before? :thinking_face:

infra-bot: Access request #AK-17111 created for user nina. Approver: @charlie. Status: pending. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-17111

ethan: welcome @nina! that Windows path means the kubeconfig you downloaded got merged with an old file from a Windows laptop (we've seen this with folks who copied configs across machines). Two fixes: 1) re-download the kubeconfig selecting the "Embed certs" option so it uses `client-certificate-data` base64 blob instead of file paths, or 2) replace the `client-certificate` / `client-key` entries with `client-certificate-data` / `client-key-data`. Example (mac):
```bash
# embed certs inline (one-liner)
kubectl config view --raw --flatten --minify > /tmp/kc && 
awk '/client-certificate:|client-key:/{next}1' /tmp/kc > /tmp/kc2 && 
# then manually add base64 data or re-download with embed option
```
If you want I can re-generate and DM you the proper blob.

nina: thanks! I don't want to paste cert blobs in chat. Is there a safe portal to re-download?

ethan: yeah use the onboarding portal -> Kubernetes Access -> Download kubeconfig -> choose "OS: macOS / Linux (OIDC + embedded certs)". That should give you a clean config with `client-certificate-data` entries.

charlie: @nina I can approve the access once your manager confirmation step goes through. Quick question: do you need `edit` in `research` or `view` only for now?

nina: edit would help for my local manifests but happy to start with view if required. Manager is copied on the invite but might be slow today.

grace: small troubleshooting tip: if after re-downloading you still see the Windows path, run `kubectl config view -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'` and inspect the `users` section. Look for `client-certificate:` vs `client-certificate-data:`. Also check `$KUBECONFIG` isn't pointing to another file (run `echo $KUBECONFIG`). Another command to just show the user entries: `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.users[*].name}'`

nina: `echo $KUBECONFIG` is empty, so defaulting to ~/.kube/config. I re-downloaded the config from onboarding as recommended and the Windows path is gone. `kubectl config view --raw` now shows `client-certificate-data`.

infra-bot: Access request #AK-17111 updated: approver @charlie notified. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-17111

charlie: approved AK-17111 for 48h onboarding (temporary `onboard-nina` binding to namespace `research` with `edit`). I'll add a note to convert to team group after your probation. @ethan can you ensure AD mapping is correct?

ethan: done, added `nina-devs` group mapping and linked your GitHub handle (nina-dev). Should be synced in a minute.

nina: confirmed `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n research` -> `yes` and `kubectl get pods -n research` works. Also created a context that defaults the namespace: `kubectl config set-context nina-research --namespace=research --cluster=redwood-dev@redwood-cluster --user=nina-oidc && kubectl config use-context nina-research`.

grace: welcome @nina! quick safety reminder: avoid running `kubectl delete` without `--dry-run=client` in team namespaces. If you need persistent access, file a ticket to move you from `onboard-nina` to the permanent `nina-devs` group after 2-4 weeks.

nina: will do, thanks everyone for the quick help :sparkles:
